content: The Stop Smoking initiative is a cognitive intervention that was launched in April 2007 as part of the QOACH (Question Oriented Approach for Common Health) program. Its primary goal is to replace the habit of smoking with the development of new learning behaviors. Dr. Alexandre-Pierre Gaspar conceptualized this project with the dual purpose of both eliminating the smoking habit and redirecting the energy associated with smoking toward acquiring new knowledge or skills. The initial method devised within the framework of the Stop Smoking project is straightforward: instead of reaching for a cigarette, the individual is encouraged to recall or engage with a piece of art, music, or culture. For instance, whenever the urge to smoke arises, the individual can access a random piece of cultural or artistic content online, thereby channeling their desire into an opportunity to learn something new. Over time, the gratification derived from learning is intended to supplant the pleasure previously associated with smoking. Currently, various adaptations of this method are being developed to accommodate different contexts and personality types, ensuring its applicability and effectiveness across diverse populations.
